elements.text: Flight crew training, experience, and applicable manual procedures were inadequate to prepare them to safely respond to adverse stall behavior encountered during the postmaintenance stall test flight.
Similarities in wing design among other airplane models on type certificate A3EU create a potential for unacceptable stall characteristics during postmaintenance stall test flights.

FAA review and approval of stall test flight information in the structural repair manual and Temporary Revision No. 28 were inadequate, failing to ensure clear and accurate instructions for incorporating information into airplane manuals.

Flight crews may not fully understand wing sensitivity to surface anomalies (e.g., imperceptible defects or light ice), leading to stalls before stick shaker/pusher activation and unpreparedness for recovery.
Owners, operators, and pilots may be unaware of the severity of unacceptable stall behavior and that required recovery training exceeds typical operational line pilot training.
Recommendation to Textron Aviation Inc. to define manufacturer-authorized pilot training and experience qualification criteria for postmaintenance stall test flights.
